environmental.acoustic-noise: 39.7 dBA with a 715 W AC AFO supply (datasheet Table 3, ISO 7779 at 23 C)
environmental.altitude: up to 3049 m operating (10,000 ft); 4877 m non-operating
environmental.humidity: 10 to 85 percent noncondensing operating; 0 to 95 percent non-operating
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 45 C (32 to 113 F) for AFO models; 0 to 35 C for AFI models

features.macsec: IEEE 802.1AE on all Gigabit Ethernet and 10 Gigabit Ethernet ports
features.optics-qsfp: 40GbE QSFP+ SR (multimode) and DAC direct-attach copper (datasheet, Supported Optics)
features.poe: all 24 ports 802.3at PoE+, up to 30 W per port
features.uplink-module: one slot; 4-port 1/10 GbE SFP+ EX-UM-4X4SFP (not part of the shipping configuration)
features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 members; the four rear QSFP+ ports are Virtual Chassis ports by default

management.console: mini-USB on the front, RJ-45 CON2 on the rear
management.lcd: 2 lines of 16 characters with Menu and Enter buttons
management.oob: MGMT RJ-45 with link activity and status lamps (rear)
management.usb: one USB port on the rear

performance.airflow-cfm: fan 22 CFM, each power supply 7.5 CFM; 59 CFM total with two supplies (datasheet)
performance.throughput: 333 Mpps wire speed for the 24-port models (datasheet)

physical.depth-no-psu: 416.1 mm (16.38 in) with no power supply or uplink module (Table 10)
physical.depth-with-uplink: 457.3 mm (18 in, 45.73 cm) with a power supply and an uplink module (Table 10)
physical.weight: 13 lb (5.9 kg) with no power supply and no fan module; 16.1 lb (7.3 kg) with one power supply and two fan modules

power.poe-budget: 550 W (datasheet Table 1); 565 W with one 715 W supply and 720 W with two (guide Table 32)
power.psu-redundancy: N+0 or N+N; up to two supplies, one is enough for the chassis

ac.description: EX4300-24P as shipped - one 715 W AC power supply (AIR OUT) in slot 0 with a cover panel over slot 1, two EX4300-FAN (AIR OUT) fan modules, and the uplink slot covered. Front-to-back airflow.

s.description: EX4300-24P-S - the spare chassis, shipped with no power supply and no fan module; either AC or DC supplies and AIR OUT or AIR IN fans are ordered separately, and the datasheet's spare-chassis matrix says which combinations are supported. The supply and fan bays are shown open.

datasheet.title: EX4300 Line of Ethernet Switches Datasheet (Juniper Networks, PDF created 2022-07-25)

description: Juniper EX4300-24P - a fixed 1RU Gigabit Ethernet access switch with 24 10/100/1000BASE-T ports, every one Power over Ethernet (PoE+), and four built-in 40-Gigabit QSFP+ ports on the rear panel that are Virtual Chassis ports by default. The front carries the 24 jacks in two stacked rows, an LCD panel with Menu and Enter buttons, three chassis status lamps, a mini-USB console port and a slot for an optional uplink module, which ships covered. The rear carries the management and console jacks, a USB port, the four QSFP+ ports, two fan modules and two power supply slots; as shipped it holds one 715 W AC power supply, front-to-back (AIR OUT) fan modules and a cover panel over the second power supply slot. The EX4300-24P-S is the same chassis with the power supplies and fan modules ordered separately. The EX4300-24T is the same front without PoE.

gaps.wanted: Where the two-hole protective earthing terminal sits on the rear panel and its hole pitch. The guide's Table 69 puts it on the rear panel with a two-hole lug and 10-32 screws, and Figure 13's right-edge screws carry no callout. A rear photograph or a dimensioned drawing settles it.

A straight-on studio photograph of the rear. The maker's image library holds none for this family, so the rear is read off the low-resolution callout figure and the supply and fan art follows the isometric drawings.

A straight-on studio photograph of the EX4300-24P front. The maker's library has the EX4300-24T and EX4300-48P; the 24P front is taken from the 24T, which the guide's shared figure and the community elevations show to be the same face.
The bracket positions of the front-mounting brackets: no figure in the guide measures them, so no ear position or kit is listed.
A library component for an LCD display; the LCD panel is a decor rectangle until one exists.
The EX-UM-4X4SFP uplink module and its ports, left for the later uplink-module slice; the bay takes only the cover panel here.
One PoE budget for the model: the datasheet gives 550 W and the guide's Table 32 565 W with one 715 W supply. Both are transcribed.

fan-leds.description: Table 29 - green when the fan module is functioning normally; unlit when it is absent, failed or of the wrong airflow

attrs.redundancy-note: Hardware guide, Fan Modules: "Both the fan modules must be installed for optimal functioning of the switch"; the switch keeps running for 30 seconds without thermal shutdown while one is replaced. The guide gives no N+1 form, so no spare fan is claimed

lcd-buttons.description: the LCD panel's Menu and Enter buttons

mgmt.mixed: how the switch is reached out of band - the mini-USB console port on the front, the RJ-45 console port, the management Ethernet port and the USB port on the rear

attrs.redundancy-note: Hardware guide, AC and DC Power Supply: two redundancy configurations, N+0 (no power is reserved) and N+N (a full second supply is reserved); one supply carries the switch and up to two seat

rj45.description: The 24 built-in 10/100/1000BASE-T PoE+ ports. rel-pos carries the number printed on the faceplate; the upper jack of a column takes the even number

status-leds.description: the three chassis status lamps right of the LCD panel

vcp.description: The four built-in 40-Gigabit QSFP+ ports on the rear panel; Virtual Chassis ports by default and usable as network ports on this model

vcp-leds.description: two lamps below each QSFP+ port, link activity and status

name: ex4300-24p

ac-psu-seating.note: The guide's AC power supply table (Table 30 and the text around it) lists 350 W, 715 W and 1100 W supplies for every EX4300 except the 48MP, and its power budget tables (Table 32 for 24 ports) work the combinations, so the bays accept all three AC ratings. This model ships with the 715 W supply (Table 1 and Table 8; datasheet Table 1).

airflow.note: Guide Tables 7, 27, 28 and 31: AIR OUT (AFO) is front-to-back and AIR IN (AFI) is back-to-front; this model ships AFO fan modules and an AFO power supply (Table 28). The guide's model tables list no AFI or DC variant of the 24-port PoE switch (only the -S chassis, which takes either), so this device has no -AFI or -DC configuration.

chassis.note: Guide Table 10 and the datasheet: height 1.72 in (4.37 cm) = 43.7 mm; width 17.36 in (44.1 cm) = 441.0 mm, "the outer edges of the front-mounting brackets extend the width to 19 in", so 441.0 is the body between the bracket flanges; depth 16.38 in (41.6 cm) with no power supply or uplink module, 17.51 in (44.47 cm) with a power supply installed and 18 in (45.73 cm) with a power supply and an uplink module. The modelled depth is 444.7 mm, the figure with the power supply fitted, as shipped; the other two are in attrs. The guide's centimetre figure for the last (45.73) is 0.1 mm from its inches (457.2): the centimetre figure is carried. 1RU.

colour.note: The face is the median of 400 pixels of bare plate between the ports and the LCD in the 24T studio photograph, #898d94. The supply and fan faces are a tone darker and their tone is taken from the community NetBox elevation (estimated); see the components.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's inventory (Table 68) ships two mounting brackets and mounting screws and says the switch mounts in a two-post or four-post rack; the datasheet lists the kits EX-4PST-RMK (four-post), EX-RMK (rack-mount) and EX-WMK (wall-mount) as separate items. No figure measures the bracket position, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. The kit's part number is recorded here for the later dedupe.

front-ports.note: 24 jacks in two stacked rows, two blocks of six columns. The dark jack cavities of the top row read, in mm from the left edge, 14.33, 28.20, 42.37, 56.24, 70.11 and 84.13 in the first block and 103.08, 116.95, 131.12, 144.99, 158.55 and 173.04 in the second (the 48P photograph reads 14.13 and 102.89 for the first columns of its first two blocks), so the column pitch is about 13.98, the registry's 13.97 ganged-jack pitch (0.550 in), and the blocks start 88.8 mm apart, a 4.98 mm gutter. Row centres read 14.9 and 29.6 mm down on the 24T photograph and 15.5 and 30.7 on the 48P one: the pooled 15.2 and 30.0 were the first draft, and the render laid over the photograph at matched scale sat 0.8 mm high, so the rows centre 16.0 and 30.8 mm down (a 14.8 step, which is also what the registry's ganged-jack notes allow for a 1U face; the registry's 12.09 is a magjack-only figure). The top row is the same part turned 180 so that its keyway is up, as the photographs show lamp tabs above the upper jacks and below the lower. Past the second block the plate is bare to the LCD panel; the guide's Figure 1 shows the same.

front-right.note: Read off the 24T photograph at 3.245 px per mm with the face's left edge at 0 and the 48P photograph at 3.29 (they agree within a millimetre): LCD window 377.2 to 412.8 x 6.8 to 16.4 mm (35.6 x 9.6); the EX4300 legend above it centred at 395.4, 4.1; Menu button centre (422.2, 9.0) and Enter button (422.2, 17.2), 6.1 mm across; three chassis status lamps at x 428.9, y 6.2, 9.9 and 13.6; a face screw each side of this block at (367.4, 12.8) and (436.0, 13.1); the mini-USB console jack at (359.7, 5.8) with CON1 printed to its left; the uplink slot opening 363.3 to 437.2 x 24.2 to 42.9 mm. Each is placed by eye on those photographs.

fru-bays.note: Two power supply bays (PSU 0, PSU 1) and two fan bays (0, 1), each seating the guide's FRU parts. Mixing AFO and AFI parts, or AC and DC, is forbidden by the guide and is left to the configuration: a bay lists every part it can take and a configuration seats a matching set. The cover panel the guide ships for an empty supply slot is seated in slot 1 as shipped. The guide says this model does not support DC supplies and that its -S spare chassis does; DC supplies are seated in the -S configuration only. No supply or fan is built into the chassis: all are FRUs.

gate-1-front.note: THE FRONT PHOTOGRAPHS PASS. ex4300-24t-front-high.jpg shows the face 1431 px across (x 33 to 1463) and 142 px down: aspect 10.08 against the stated 441.0 / 43.7 = 10.09, so it is near-orthographic and carries geometry, at 3.245 px per mm; the 48P photograph is 1452 by 144 px, 3.29 px per mm. Positions are good to about half a millimetre. The two photographs give the same column centres to 0.2 mm, the second image the pitch is measured against. The guide's front figure (Figure 1) is a perspective drawing and gives counts only. No photograph of the EX4300-24P front itself was found; the guide's Figures 1 and 2 are captioned for the 24-port EX4300 switches without distinguishing the PoE model, and the NetBox EX4300-24P and EX4300-24T elevations show the same face.

gate-1-rear.note: THE REAR CALLOUT FIGURE PASSES. Guide Figure 13 (g022074) is a flat rear elevation: rendered at 600 dpi its chassis outline is 1950 x 194 px, aspect 10.05 against 10.09, 4.42 px per mm. Positions on the rear are fractions off it, good to about half a millimetre; it is a low-resolution raster.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. The guide's configuration examples name the 48-port switch's jacks ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/47 and the uplink module's ports ge-0/2/0 to ge-0/2/3 and xe-0/2/0 to xe-0/2/3; the 24-port range ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/23 follows by the same rule and is not stated. The built-in QSFP+ ports' names are stated nowhere held. No table gives the numbering rule, so the names stay out of the file as a block and go here.

lamp-legends.note: drawing-vs-photo, and the PHOTOGRAPH wins: the guide says the three chassis lamps are labeled ALM, SYS and MST, but both photographs show three bare lamps with no legend beside them. The CON1 legend, about the same height, resolves in the same photograph, so the silence is a reading and not the image's limit. No legend is drawn. The order top to bottom is the guide's order of naming (ALM, SYS, MST); no document states it, so it is estimated.

lcd.note: The LCD panel shows two lines of 16 characters (guide, LCD Panel in EX4300 Switches). It is drawn as the dark green window the photograph shows; no library component exists for a display and none is added, so it is a decor rectangle and not a part.

lifecycle.note: Searched Juniper's end-of-life notices and third-party trackers on 2026-10-21. Trackers list end-of-life notices for the EX4300-32F (last order 2026-03-31) and the EX4300-48MP (last order 2026-12-29) and for older bundle SKUs (2020), and none for the EX4300-24T, -24P, -48T or -48P; Juniper's own milestones page did not render for the search, so the absence is unconfirmed. Recorded as none-announced.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat: the guide's front and rear figures show them in perspective with a logo on the lid and mounting holes in the sides. Each carries an `empty` sentence.

port-lamps.note: Guide, Network Port, Built-In QSFP+ Port, Uplink Port, and Uplink Module Port LEDs, Figure 30 and Tables 21 and 22: each 10/100/1000BASE-T port has two lamps, a Link activity lamp (green, blinking with activity, steady when linked) and a Status lamp whose meaning is chosen with the LCD Enter button (ADM, DPX, SPD or POE on a PoE model). The lamps are the jack housing's two corner windows (common/rj45-ganged-eth) and carry that component's default vocabulary. Which window is which on this hardware is not stated by any document held, so the pairing is the component's convention.

port-numbering.note: The photograph prints the numbers in pairs under each column: 0 and 1 under the first column, 2 and 3 under the second, up to 22 and 23, with the even number set higher and the odd lower beside it. The even number belongs to the upper jack and the odd to the lower, so numbering runs down each column and then across. The guide's CLI interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled; the photograph prints no block legends.

power.note: Guide Table 32: the base power the system needs before PoE is 150 W for a 24-port switch; with one 715 W supply 565 W is available for PoE and 18 ports can be enabled, and with two 715 W supplies 720 W and all 24 ports. The datasheet's Table 1 gives the PoE budget as 550 W. Both are transcribed and not reconciled: they are two documents' statements of a PoE budget. No typical or maximum draw of the switch itself is stated by either document.

rear.note: Guide Figure 13 (g022074), 4.42 px per mm, rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing: MGMT and CON2 jacks stacked at 9.7 to 25.5 mm (centres y 16.6 and 30.8), the ESD point at (36.2, 8.4), the vertical USB port at (35.1, 28.7), fan module 0 from 49.1 to 97.7, four QSFP+ ports from 108.0 to 183.5 on the registry's 19.0 mm pitch (the figure's separators read 107.9, 127.4, 146.8, 165.8 and 184.3), fan slot numbers beside the block, fan module 1 from 194.9 to 243.5, power supply slot 0 from 257.5 and slot 1 from 348.9 (module edges found in the 600 dpi figure at 257.3 and 348.7), each 84.0 mm wide, and a strip at the right edge. The serial number label (callout 4) sits at 101.3 to 123.2 x 13.6 to 18.1. The figure is shared by the 24-port and 48-port models.

rear-ground.note: The guide says the protective earthing terminal of the EX4300 is on the rear panel (Table 69: two-hole terminal, two 10-32 screws, Panduit LCD10-10A-L lug) but no figure identifies it or gives its pitch, and the rear-panel figure's right-edge screws are not named by a callout. It is not modelled; see gaps.

rear-qsfp-lamps.note: Guide Figure 13 callout 11 and Figure 32: each QSFP+ port has two lamps below it, a Link activity lamp and a Status lamp (Table 24: steady green when the 40-Gigabit port is up). Eight small rectangles below the block at y 39.6, each pair 7.4 mm apart about its port's centre. The lamps' roles within a pair are not stated.

sources.note: EX4300 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2025-08-12 (414 pages; https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4300/ex4300.pdf): Figures 1 and 2 (24-port panel drawings), Figures 9 and 13 (callouts), Table 1 and Table 8 (models and what each ships with), Table 10 (chassis size and weight), Tables 18 to 26 (LEDs), Tables 27, 28, 30, 31, 40-42, 47, 48 (fans and supplies), Table 32 (power budget) and Table 68 (cover panels). EX4300 Line of Ethernet Switches Datasheet (https://www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets/us/en/switches/ex4300-line-of-ethernet-switches-datasheet.pdf, 17 pages, PDF created 2022-07-25): Table 1 (models), Table 2 (spare chassis), Table 3 (acoustics), physical and environmental specifications, ordering information. Juniper's straight-on studio photographs ex4300-24t-front-high.jpg (1500 x 195 px, the non-PoE sibling, whose front is the same) and ex4300-48p-front-high.jpg (1500 x 211 px) from its image library. The NetBox device-type library's EX4300-24P, 24T and 48P elevations (community drawings, not the maker's) were used only to cross-check counts and which side a feature sits. The guide's own panel figures are isometric drawings, so every front position is read off a straight-on photograph and every rear position off the flat callout figure. No studio photograph of the rear exists: the image library has front shots only. Terms of use: the guide, datasheet and photographs are Juniper's, published for customers; none is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

uplink-slot.note: Every EX4300 24-port and 48-port switch has one front-panel uplink module slot (guide, Uplink Modules in EX4300 Switches); uplink modules are not part of the shipping configuration and the guide's inventory (Table 68) says a cover panel for the slot is provided. The slot is a bay that takes the cover panel here; the EX-UM-4X4SFP module it is sold with is left for a later slice. The photographs are of switches with a module fitted, so they give the opening and not the cover.

references.title: EX4300 Switch Hardware Guide (Juniper Networks, published 2025-08-12)

bottom.empty: Not drawn by any source held: neither the guide nor the datasheet pictures the underside (the guide lists four rubber feet in its inventory, Table 68).

placements.description: Table 18 - ALM: red major alarm, yellow minor alarm, unlit no alarm (red at power-up until a network link is made)
Table 18 - SYS: green steady, Junos OS loaded; green blinking, booting; unlit, powered off or halted
Table 18 - MST: standalone, green steady when functioning; Virtual Chassis, green steady primary, blinking backup, unlit line card

left.empty: Not drawn flat by any source held. The guide's perspective figures show the left side wall with mounting holes, and the front-mounting brackets are separate hardware.

placements.description: Tables 19 and 20 - Link/Activity green blinking with activity, steady without; Status green steady at 1000 Mbps, blinking at 100 Mbps, off at 10 Mbps

right.empty: Not drawn flat by any source held. The guide's perspective figures show the right side wall with mounting holes.

top.empty: Not drawn flat by any source held. The guide's Figures 1 and 2 show the lid in perspective with a logo and mounting holes along the sides; nothing there can be measured.
